capability: Import and export of store data: products, customers and orders (Salla Import & export / إدارة الاستيراد والتصدير, Exports / التصدير; Shopify product imports and the Export permissions)
note: Parent of CM-MIG-002 and CM-MIG-003. Neither platform keeps one section for import and export: Salla puts each object's import or export in that object's list (products, customers, orders) and holds them under one staff permission, import_export_management, one flag, impex, and one Merchant API folder, Exports; Shopify puts its product import routes in Products and an Export permission under each object's section. The objects are named in the cells' readings, not split into capabilities, since each object's section belongs to another domain. Homonyms kept out: customs import and export (duties, export control), the export of a customer's personal data (privacy), marketplace order import (channels).

capability: Advanced import (Salla Advanced import / الاستيراد المتقدم, its custom importer)
note: Salla gives it its own link, route and dashboard app (/importer) and permissions apart from import_export_management. The parent is by its own name, an import (إدارة الاستيراد المتقدم), listed in the products list beside Import & export. Salla doesn't say what it imports or how it differs from Import & export.

capability: Export templates (Salla Export templates, for products and orders)
note: Salla's own links put the templates at the products' and orders' exports routes (/products/exports, /orders/exports). What a template holds isn't stated.

capability: Export log: the record of a store's exports (Salla Export log / سجل التصدير)
note: No parent: Salla's route puts it under its logs (/logs/export), beside Activity history (SA-C-010, domain A's audit log), which a parent in this domain can't follow. Homonym: Salla's سجل names both this export log and the activity log (سجل العمليات), and Q1 lists logs as audit logs against system logs (U-044); this capability is neither.

capability: Moving a store from another platform (Salla's store migration service / خدمة انتقال المتاجر من منصات أخرى; Shopify's migrating from QuickBooks Desktop POS)
note: Salla keeps the service apart from import and export: it has its own terms, eligibility, benefits and contracting company. No platform statement puts it under import and export, so it has no parent.

capability: Platform reliability and continuity: staying available under load, through failures, and when a partner fails (Salla استقرار المنصة وجاهزيتها للذروة; Shopify pods and recovery sites)
note: Joined on role, a reading: Salla sells platform stability and readiness for peak as a plan line, and Shopify's engineering statements describe isolated pods, each with a recovery site. Neither defines the term. What happens when a partner fails (SA-C-235) sits here because no platform gives it a place of its own (convention 2); its statements are each about one kind of partner.
Salla's status page lists components with their state (Merchant APIs; Store APIs, SA-C-101, is domain E's). The concern map holds no Shopify status page.
